scenario.name: CISA ICS-ALERT-17-356-01, Mandiant & Dragos — TRISIS / TRITON Safety Instrumented System (SIS) TriStation Protocol Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a bustling coastal shipping port with blue harbor water, stacked colorful steel cargo containers, a towering yellow overhead gantry crane, and a moored cargo ship. Out on the concrete harbor pier, a worker notices a single shipping container whose side inspection hatch was accidentally left unlatched during loading. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the harbor customs inspector's station, then smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches. The port authority watchtower spots footsteps leaving a supposedly sealed container bay and compares the manifest seal numbers against the pier camera. In this scenario (T1036.005, CISA ICS-ALERT-17-356-01, Mandiant & Dragos, TRISIS / TRITON Safety Instrumented System , SIS TriStation Protocol Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: masqueraded Py2EXE Binary, then triStation Protocol UDP 1502 Ping, then triStation Program Allocation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Masqueraded Py2EXE Binary, then TriStation Protocol UDP 1502 Ping, then TriStation Program Allocation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 2: TriStation Protocol UDP 1502 Ping & Controller Program Mode Status Check
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1082 - System Information Discovery / SIS Keyswitch Status)
stages.description: Slipping out through that open container hatch while the yellow gantry crane swings overhead, the stowaway steps straight onto the restricted customs dockyard. Here in Step 2 inside the shipping port, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the sealed bonded export yard. The TsLow.py module transmits a UDP port 1502 TriStation connect/ping packet to the Triconex controller and queries the front-panel keyswitch state, verifying whether the physical keyswitch is left in PROGRAM mode (which permits memory/program modifications) (logged in Network Event 1502 with Protocol=Triconex TriStation , UDP 1502, CommandCode=GetCpStatus , Controller Status Query, KeyswitchPosition=PROGRAM Mode , Remote Write Permitted so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes tshark -r sis-network.pcap -Y "udp.port == 1502" -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e data.data (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , tshark -r sis-network.pcap -Y "udp.port == 1502" -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e data.data so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1082 during "TriStation Protocol UDP 1502 Ping & Controller Program Mode Status Check" , The TsLow while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ TriStation UDP/1502 Function=GetCpStatus KeyswitchState=PROGRAM / ⇠#2 RESP 1502) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 UDP 1502 TriStation Link), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Physical Keyswitch (PROGRAM Mode)).

stages.title: Stage 3: TriStation Program Allocation & Triple-Modular Redundant (TMR) Validation Check
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1542 - Pre-OS Boot / Controller Firmware & Logic Modification)
stages.description: Now roaming freely outside the sealed steel box, the intruder walks across the shipping port pier and alters manifests bound for the moored cargo ship. In this final step inside the shipping port, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches until the port authority manifest watch catches the mismatch. When an unauthorized program table modification (inject.bin / imain.bin) is transmitted over UDP 1502, the Triconex Triple-Modular Redundant (TMR) processors compare memory state across the three independent main processor legs and log a diagnostic fault if a validation mismatch occurs (logged in IDS Alert Event 35601 with AlertSignature=CISA ICS-ALERT-17-356-01 , TRISIS / TRITON TriStation Write, TargetArchitecture=MPC860 PowerPC Triple-Modular Redundant , TMR, TelemetrySource=Passive OT Span Port Sensor so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes snort -c /etc/snort/tristation-cisa-17-356.rules -r sis-network.pcap (which Captures or inspects industrial control system , ICS/OT protocol frames and engineering workstation logs , snort -c /etc/snort/tristation-cisa-17-3 so that reconstructs PLC logic transfers, substation breaker telecontrol commands, or Safety Instrumented System , SIS controller state changes , T1542 during "TriStation Program Allocation & Triple-Modular Redundant , TMR Validation Check"). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ ALERT CISA-ICS-17-356-01 TriStation Unauthorized Function Table Write on UDP 1502 / ⇠#3 ALERT 35601) from Node ③ (#3 UDP 1502 TriStation Link) to Node ④ (#4 Triconex SIS Controller (MPC860)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Physical Keyswitch (PROGRAM Mode)).
